fromVietnamese.Định ngữ (관형사형) là cách biến động từ/tín:
The noun-modifying form (관형사형) turns a verb or adjective into a word or clause placed BEFORE a noun. Vietnamese usually puts the noun before its adjective; Korean puts the modifier first, as in 예쁜 꽃.

• Adjective + (으)ㄴ: describes a noun's current quality or state. 작은 집 (a small house), 좋은 사람 (a good person), 바쁜 하루 (a busy day).
• Verb + 는: describes an ongoing or habitual action. 읽는 책 (the book being read), 다니는 회사 (the company one works for), 자주 가는 식당 (a restaurant one often visits).
• 있다/없다 and compounds such as 맛있다, 맛없다, 재미있다, 재미없다 use the verb ending 는 in this form: 맛있는 음식, 재미있는 영화.

Irregular forms to remember with (으)ㄴ:
• Stems ending in ㄹ drop ㄹ before ㄴ/는: 살다 → 사는, 길다 → 긴, 멀다 → 먼.
• Stems ending in ㅂ: ㅂ → 우, as in 덥다 → 더운, 어렵다 → 어려운, 귀엽다 → 귀여운.
• Stems ending in ㅎ drop ㅎ: 그렇다 → 그런, 어떻다 → 어떤, 하얗다 → 하얀.
fromVietnamese.Dùng mỗi khi muốn mô tả danh từ bằng một:
Use whenever you want to describe a noun with a word or a whole clause. The phrase [determinant + noun] then acts like a normal noun, with particles 이/가, 을/를, 에… attached behind it.

Compare to clearly see the role:
• 꽃이 예뻐요. = Beautiful flowers. (예쁘다 as predicate, ends sentence)
• 예쁜 꽃을 샀어요. = I bought beautiful flowers. (예쁜 as determiner for 꽃)

The subject inside the determiner clause uses 이/가 (don't use 은/는): 제가 읽는 책 = the book I'm reading.

The determiner also has a past form. V-(으)ㄴ, future V-(으)ㄹ and retrospective -던 — see separate articles in TOPIK II section.

Most confusing point: same ending (으)ㄴ but different meaning depending on the type of word:
• ADJECTIVE + (으)ㄴ = present: 예쁜 꽃 (beautiful flower — now).
• VERB + (으)ㄴ = past: 먹은 음식 (the food was eaten — already).
So when encountering the form (으)ㄴ, you must determine whether the root is a verb or an adjective to translate it correctly.

• 지금 읽는 책 = book being read (present)
• 내일 읽을 책 = book to read tomorrow (future)

fromVietnamese.Định ngữ tương lai: hành động sẽ xảy ra:
Future determiner: action that will happen or is planned to do, modifies the following noun ('… will/to/need…'). 내일 입을 옷 = the outfit (to be) worn tomorrow; 먹을 것 = food to eat.

This is the form of determiner that appears the most in the grammar samples we have learned — in fact, they are all [V-(으)ㄹ + noun]:
• -(으)ㄹ 거예요 = ㄹ + 것 (thing to do) → equivalent hybrid
• -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = ㄹ + 수 (way/ability) → can
• -(으)ㄹ 때 = ㄹ + 때 (at) → when…
• -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다 = ㄹ + 줄 (how to do) → know how
Understanding the predicate ㄹ is understanding the root of the above series of sentences.

In addition to the future meaning, V-(으)ㄹ also describes things that have NOT happened yet in general. (intended, need to be done): 할 일 = something to do, 마실 물 = water to drink.
fromVietnamese.Dùng khi danh từ được mô tả bằng hành độ:
Used when the noun is described by an action that has not yet/is about to happen: plan (내일 만날 사람 = person to meet tomorrow), purpose (먹을 것, 읽을 책), to-do (오늘 할 일).

Note on spelling/pronunciation: after the determiner ㄹ, the first consonant of the noun The next word is often tense when speaking: 할 것 is read as [할 껏], 갈 데 is read as [갈 떼].

Quick comparison of 3 tenses: 읽은 책 (read) · 읽는 책 (reading) · 읽을 책 (will read).
I have prepared clothes to wear tomorrow.
There's a lot to do today.
There's nothing to eat in the refrigerator.

fromVietnamese.Định ngữ hồi tưởng, dùng khi nhớ lại quá:
The adjective reminiscence, used when remembering the past to describe a noun. There are two forms with different nuances:

① -던: regular REPEATING action/state in the past ('that time was good…'), or UNFINISHED action ('was… then abandoned').
• 자주 가던 카페 = the coffee shop that I used to go to at that time (past habit)
• 마시던 커피 = unfinished cup of coffee (not finished drinking)

② -았던/었던: something that was COMPLETED in the past, often implying that it is no longer like that, only in memory.
• 어렸을 때 살았던 집 = the house where you lived as a child (now you don't live anymore)
• 예뻤던 그 거리 = the street used to be very beautiful (now it may be different)

Distinguish between 3 ways of saying 'read book':
• 읽은 책: finished reading — neutral information.
• 읽던 책: in progress — not finished, can read continued.
• 읽었던 책: once read (a long time ago) — emphasizes recollection.
fromVietnamese.Dùng -던 khi kể về thói quen, kỷ niệm tro:
Use -던 when talking about past habits and memories (usually with 자주, 옛날에, 어렸을 때...) or unfinished tasks.

Use -았던/었던 when the task has completely ended and the speaker is reminiscing; adjectives that want to talk about past states must use this form or -던 (adjectives do NOT have their own past deterministic form (으)ㄴ — 예쁜 is always present, if you want to say 'used to be beautiful', you must use 예쁘던/예뻤던).

In Korean songs, poems, and memoirs, -던 appears a lot because of its nostalgic nuance.
It's the park I used to go to when I was little.

fromVietnamese.Quy tắc chia thì hiện tại thân mật. Xét: To conjugate the informal polite present tense, remove 다 and look at the stem's last vowel, rather than its 받침. Vowels often contract when the ending is added.
fromVietnamese.Bỏ 다 lấy gốc, thêm 아요/어요 theo nguyên âm: Remove 다 to get the root, add 아요/어요 according to the last vowel, then shorten if necessary.
fromVietnamese.Gốc có 받침 + 으(세요/면/ㄹ…) · Gốc không 받침 →: Root has 받침 + 으(세요/면/ㄹ…) · Root does not 받침 → remove 으
fromVietnamese.Nhiều đuôi bắt đầu bằng (으): -(으)세요, -(으: Many endings start with (으): -(으)세요, -(으)면, -(으)ㄹ, -(으)러... If there is 받침 then keep 으, if not 받침 then drop it.
fromVietnamese.Kiểm tra 받침 của âm tiết cuối gốc để quyế: Check the 받침 of the root-final syllable to decide whether to keep or drop 으.
fromVietnamese.받침 ㅂ + nguyên âm → 우 (ㅂ + 아/어 → 워): 받침 ㅂ + vowel → 우 (ㅂ + 아/어 → 워)
fromVietnamese.Phần lớn tính từ có 받침 ㅂ: ㅂ đổi thành 우: Most adjectives ending in 받침 ㅂ change ㅂ to 우 before a vowel. 돕다/곱다 are exceptions that form 와.
fromVietnamese.Áp dụng cho 덥다, 춥다, 쉽다, 어렵다, 맵다… Ngoại l: Applies to 덥다, 춥다, 쉽다, 어렵다, 맵다… Exception: 돕다→도와요, 곱다→고와요.
fromVietnamese.Một số động từ có 받침 ㄷ đổi thành ㄹ khi g: Some verbs have 받침 ㄷ changed to ㄹ when encountering vowels. Many other verbs are still regular.
fromVietnamese.Bất quy tắc: 듣다, 걷다, 묻다(hỏi), 싣다. Quy tắ: Irregular: 듣다, 걷다, 묻다(ask), 싣다. Rules: 받다, 닫다, 믿다.
fromVietnamese.받침 ㅅ + nguyên âm → ㅅ rụng (KHÔNG rút gọn: 받침 ㅅ + vowel → ㅅ dropped (DO NOT shorten vowel)
fromVietnamese.Một số động từ rụng 받침 ㅅ khi gặp nguyên: Some verbs drop 받침 ㅅ when they encounter a vowel, but the vowel is not shortened.
fromVietnamese.Bất quy tắc: 짓다, 낫다, 붓다, 젓다. Quy tắc: 웃다: Irregularities: 짓다, 낫다, 붓다, 젓다. Rules: 웃다, 씻다, 벗다.
fromVietnamese.Gốc kết thúc ㅡ + 아/어 → ㅡ rụng; nguyên âm: Terminating stem ㅡ + 아/어 → ㅡ falls off; vowel before decision 아/어
fromVietnamese.Gốc có nguyên âm cuối ㅡ thì rụng ㅡ khi t: The root with the final vowel ㅡ loses ㅡ when adding 아/어요. Consider the vowel of the immediately preceding syllable (ㅏ/ㅗ → 아, remaining → 어); If there is only one syllable, use 어.
fromVietnamese.Áp dụng cho 쓰다, 크다, 바쁘다, 예쁘다, 아프다, 배고프다…: Applicable to 쓰다, 크다, 바쁘다, 예쁘다, 아프다, 배고프다…
fromVietnamese.Gốc kết thúc 르 + 아/어 → thêm ㄹ (르 → ㄹ라 /: End stem 르 + 아/어 → add ㄹ (르 → ㄹ라 / ㄹ러)
fromVietnamese.Gốc kết thúc 르: khi gặp 아/어, ㅡ rụng và t: A stem ending in 르 drops ㅡ before 아/어 and adds ㄹ to the preceding syllable. Use ㄹ라 if the preceding vowel is ㅏ/ㅗ, and ㄹ러 otherwise.
fromVietnamese.Áp dụng cho 모르다, 다르다, 빠르다, 부르다, 자르다…: Applicable to 모르다, 다르다, 빠르다, 부르다, 자르다…
fromVietnamese.받침 ㄹ + đuôi bắt đầu ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ → ㄹ rụng: 받침 ㄹ + tail begins ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ → ㄹ falls off
fromVietnamese.Gốc có 받침 ㄹ thì rụng ㄹ trước các đuôi bắ: The root with 받침 ㄹ drops ㄹ before the endings starting with ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (eg -ㅂ니다, -세요, -는). Keep ㄹ before the vowel.
fromVietnamese.Áp dụng cho 살다, 만들다, 알다, 팔다, 열다…: Applicable to 살다, 만들다, 알다, 팔다, 열다…
fromVietnamese.Tính từ có 받침 ㅎ + nguyên âm → ㅎ rụng, ng: Adjectives with 받침 ㅎ + vowel → ㅎ falls out, vowel changes to 애/에
fromVietnamese.Đa số tính từ chỉ màu/trạng thái có 받침 ㅎ: Most color or state adjectives ending in 받침 ㅎ drop ㅎ and change the vowel (아/어 → 애). 좋다 follows the regular pattern.
fromVietnamese.Áp dụng cho 그렇다, 빨갛다, 파랗다, 어떻다, 하얗다. Quy: Applies to 그렇다, 빨갛다, 파랗다, 어떻다, 하얗다. Rules: 좋다, 놓다, 넣다.

fromVietnamese.Sau các 받침 tắc ㄱ,ㄷ,ㅂ, phụ âm đầu tiếp th: After the 받침 stops ㄱ,ㄷ,ㅂ, the next initial consonant is pronounced tense.
fromVietnamese.Khi ㅎ gặp ㄱ,ㄷ,ㅂ,ㅈ (trước hoặc sau), hai: When ㅎ meets ㄱ,ㄷ,ㅂ,ㅈ (before or after), the two sounds combine to form the corresponding aspirated consonant.
fromVietnamese.받침 ㅎ khi đứng trước nguyên âm thì không: 받침 ㅎ is not read when standing before a vowel.

fromVietnamese.Hệ số gốc Hán, dùng cho tiền (원), tháng: The Sino-Korean number system comes from Chinese. Use it for money (원), months (월), dates (일), minutes (분), telephone numbers, ordinal numbers and large numbers.
fromVietnamese.Ghép: hàng chục + hàng đơn vị (이십오 = 25): Pairing: tens + units (이십오 = 25). Used with 원/월/일/분/번…

fromVietnamese.Trước đơn vị, các số này biến đổi: 하나→한,: Before the unit, these numbers vary: 하나→한, 둘→두, 셋→세, 넷→네, 스물→스무.
